subject: Urgent: Streaming response slowdown — temporary mitigations & post-incident plan
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Svensson <anna.svensson@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Urgent: Streaming response slowdown — temporary mitigations & post-incident plan

Hi Anna —

We observed elevated tail latency for streaming/chat responses affecting a subset of EU realtime edge nodes beginning ~2026-11-19T07:45Z and lasting through the morning. Impacts you may see: audio/chat/video-style streaming sessions where partial chunks delay or pause for 1–4s intermittently, and occasional aborted streams.

Quick summary:
- Affected endpoints: /v1/chat/stream and websocket-based realtime in eu-west-1 region.
- Root cause (ongoing investigation): transient KV cache warmup failure combined with a routing imbalance that increased load on a small set of inference shards.
- Scope: ~2–6% of customer streaming sessions in EU; non-streaming generation (non-stream mode) not materially affected.

Temporary mitigations you can apply immediately (client-side):
1) Switch to non-streaming (response_mode: "non_stream") for high-criticality flows while we stabilize (expect slightly higher end-to-end latency but consistent responses).
2) For WebSocket clients: implement short reconnect backoff (250ms -> 2s) and enable resume-on-disconnect (send last_token_id to resume).
3) Reduce max_tokens per incremental request (e.g., limit to 256) and split larger responses server-side.

Server-side / Redwood actions we are taking now:
- Applying a temporary routing policy to shift new streaming requests to warmed shards and enable KV warmup preloads for FinLytics traffic. (Ben taking lead)
- Uploading telemetry snapshot and creating a short-term cache warmup job. (Marissa)
- Preparing a customer-specific workaround doc and a short code snippet you can paste into your SDK. (Olga)

I've attached a short workaround playbook and the telemetry snapshot we captured. We'll follow up with an ETA for the full postmortem once the investigation completes. If you'd like, we can jump on a 30-min call this morning to walk through the changes.

Short-term ask: Can your team enable a non-streaming fallback for 1–2 hours as a safeguard? If yes, reply with a preferred time window and whether you need code samples for your client.

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov

Subject: Re: Urgent: Streaming response slowdown — temporary mitigations & post-incident plan

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the heads up and the playbook. We can enable a non-streaming fallback, but several of our UX flows rely on WebSocket resume to avoid a full refresh. Two quick questions:

1) Is there a short code snippet you recommend for resume-on-disconnect? We currently keep a rolling last_token_id per session and would rather not re-request the entire history.
2) What is the expected change in token-cost if we switch to non-streaming for the next 1–2 hours?

We'd like to try a fallback window starting at 09:00 UTC if that aligns with your planned routing adjustments.

—Anna
Anna Svensson

Ben / Olga —

Telemetry quick notes:
- During the window 07:45–08:30Z, a small fraction of shards (3/48) experienced elevated KV miss rates, which caused prefix cache stalls. That combined with a routing weight spike pushed CPU on those hosts above our soft-sla threshold, causing token emission jitter.
- We captured span traces tied to FinLytics sessions (attached snapshot). No data exfiltration or persistent error rates on non-stream endpoints.

Proposed immediate actions (I can execute 1 and 3):
1) Deploy a temporary routing override for FinLytics traffic to route 80% of new streaming requests to warmed shards and 20% to regular pool. (Ben: please deploy via routing console ASAP.)
2) Trigger KV prewarm for hotspot prefixes seen in the snapshot. (Platform: needs a short job; ETA ~25m.)
3) Publish a short customer-facing runbook and snippet for resume-on-disconnect and non-stream fallback. (Olga: I can draft then you can send.)
4) Schedule a follow-up postmortem doc and 30-min customer sync for tomorrow. I'll upload traces and highlight mitigation timelines.

I'll attach the telemetry file to our internal incident and link the postmortem doc here after initial upload.

—Marissa
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Svensson <anna.svensson@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Urgent: Streaming response slowdown — temporary mitigations & post-incident plan

Hi Anna —

Thanks for the quick reply. We applied the temporary routing override at 08:58Z (policy id: finlytics-temp-eu-20261119) and verified KV prewarm kicked off; you should see reduced pause frequency immediately on new sessions.

Answers to your questions:
1) Resume snippet (WebSocket):
   - On disconnect, send: { "cmd": "resume", "last_token_id": <last_token_id> }
   - Server will reply with "resume_ack" and stream missing tokens. This avoids re-requesting full context. See attached workaround-snippet.txt.
2) Cost delta for non-streaming: switching to non-streaming increases per-request tokenization latency but the token consumption is essentially identical — cost changes are negligible (estimate +0–3% for typical sessions).

Next steps:
- Can you enable the non-streaming fallback between 09:00–11:00 UTC as a precaution? We will monitor closely and revert when metrics stabilize.
- We'll host a 30-min post-incident review tomorrow at 09:30 UTC; invite to follow.

Link to postmortem (draft): https://drive.redwood.ai/postmortems/RE-2026-11-19-realtime-pulse

If you want me to patch a small SDK example into your repo, I can send a PR with the snippet.

Regards,
Olga
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
